v1.feedback: The Shiota thread-room reads instantly — 20k lines converging on a suspended translucent sphere is a strong silhouette, and the warm-black-to-crimson palette is exactly the restraint the gallery rewards. The periodic pulse sells 'soft-erupt' but could hit harder: try ramping the sphere's emissive from near-zero to a brief warm bloom (0.9→0.15 over ~1.5s) so the erupt feels like an exhale rather than a sine wobble. The fog at 0.014 eats the far wall-to-wall threads that give Shiota pieces their claustrophobic tension — drop it to ~0.006 so the room envelope stays legible. Consider thinning the dendritic branching density by 30% near the sphere surface so the object's silhouette stays crisp against the web.

v2.feedback: Strong execution of 'soft-erupt' — the piece builds a Chiharu Shiota-inspired thread installation around a pale suspended sphere, then periodically erupts it with wave-based displacement that creates delightful droop/sag in outer threads while inner threads stay taut. The restrained palette (pale sphere, dark umber threads, warm fog) and readable form earn high marks. Minor nitpick: the eruption could have slightly more amplitude (currently ~0.9 units max) to make the 'swerve' more visceral, and the dendritic pruning near the sphere (added post-critique) slightly over-thins the shell in some views — dial back the 0.30 skip rate to 0.18 for better volume.
